newsitem.title: USA: Abducted Michigan schoolgirls seen in Florida - FBI.
newsitem.headline: Abducted Michigan schoolgirls seen in Florida - FBI.

text.p: Two young sisters who disappeared on Friday after stepping off a school bus were spotted in Florida over the weekend with the three men suspected of kidnapping them, the FBI said on Monday.
Teresa and Jessica Hainer of Galesburg, Mich., have been the subject of a nationwide search by law enforcement since they got into a station wagon occupied by three men after school on Friday.
FBI Special Agent Thomas Bailey said an off-duty police officer spotted the girls, the car and the kidnapping suspects at a car wash in Gainesville, Fla., at about noon on Sunday.
"He recognised them from the news reports," Bailey said. "We feel very confident that we have a sighting."

Arrest warrants were issued on Saturday against three people who police believe to be familiar with the girls and their father, Jessie Hainer, who was separated from the girls' mother and with whom they lived.
Bailey said the federal warrants charge Ronald Stafford, 21, Ricky Geer, 19, and an unidentified 17-year-old male with kidnapping.

"The girls know them and they know the girls," Bailey said, adding that when they were spotted on Sunday, they appeared "disheveled" and were wearing different clothing from what they were wearing when they were last seen.

Teresa, 9, and Jessica, 6, were supposed to go to a baby sitter's home when they were dropped off in a trailer park in western Michigan, near Kalamazoo, but got into a cream-coloured 1988 Pontiac 6000 station wagon with wood-grain side panels and Michigan license plate number 1AX-J93.
Bailey said law enforcement agencies were searching intensely in the Southeast, but were not limiting the effort to that region.

"One of our big concerns is that Gainesville is on the I-75 corridor," he said. "They were spotted at noon (Sunday), and that's more than 24 hours ago. They could be quite a long distance from there."
